newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan auto body says doesn't want dollar firming.
newsitem.headline: Japan auto body says doesn't want dollar firming.

text.p: Takao Tominaga, vice chairman and executive managing director of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA), told Reuters on Thursday he does not want to see the dollar strengthening from the current level.

Asked about the JAMA chairman's remarks in June that the appropriate level for the dollar against the yen was in the range of 105 to 115 yen to the dollar, he said: "At the moment, I guess the JAMA chairman probably sees an appropriate dollar/yen level of 110 to 120."
About about whether the current 118 yen/dollar level was an appropriate level, he said: "Yes."
"Due to the trade issue, I do not want a weaker yen," he told Reuters after a luncheon speech.
Tominaga also said he does not expect Japan's vehicle exports to keep rising at the current pace.
"I do not think exports will continue at the current speed."
